nodes.title: Triangular Diplomacy
nodes.description: Open parallel American channels to Beijing and Moscow. Economic access, strategic consultation and selective commitments give Washington several ways to negotiate.
nodes.strategy: Build two useful alternatives before choosing where to concentrate American commitments.
requirements: The existing Kissinger foreign-policy entry.
effects: Existing entry to both diplomatic channels.

nodes.title: A Channel to Beijing
nodes.description: Establish a confidential American channel to the Chinese government. Political contact can continue alongside negotiations with Moscow.
nodes.strategy: Create a credible alternative to exclusive reliance on Soviet negotiations.
requirements: China exists and can receive the proposal.

nodes.title: Détente with Moscow
nodes.description: Bring regular consultations with Moscow into the existing bilateral negotiating channel. Washington prepares a Nuclear Risk Reduction paper; the Soviet government reviews, revises or signs the actual terms.
nodes.strategy: Keep Moscow interested in cooperation while Washington also speaks to Beijing.
requirements: The Soviet Union exists and is at peace with the United States.
Both governments sign the same reviewed paper.
nodes.history: Existing entry; proposed integration with standing treaty negotiations
effects: Unlocks the Nuclear Risk Reduction negotiating initiative.

treaty.term: Until withdrawal; other treaty terms remain negotiable.
treaty.lifecycle: An existing signed accord is recognised. A paper awaiting signature remains with its delegations.

nodes.title: Trade and Exchanges
nodes.description: Offer a four-year trade and production-exchange programme. American access to Chinese consumer goods reduces the civilian industry reserved for consumer demand, while production exchanges accelerate Chinese productivity growth. Both governments benefit from maintaining the opening.
nodes.strategy: Secure an American economic benefit while giving China a four-year development incentive to preserve its relationship with Washington.
requirements: An accepted Beijing Backchannel.
China accepts the four-year trade and production-exchange programme.
nodes.history: Historical trade-opening precedent; proposed four-year economic benefits

nodes.title: Bilateral Cooperation
nodes.description: Offer a scientific programme alongside a bilateral investment protocol. Both delegations review the research benefits, investment discounts and programme funding in the same negotiating paper.
nodes.strategy: Create an economic and institutional stake in continued negotiations with Washington.
requirements: The American-Soviet negotiating channel is open.
The investment paper includes the scientific programme and both governments sign it.

treaty.lifecycle: Research benefits and weekly funding require the signed scientific programme and continuing joint participation.

nodes.title: Play the China Card
nodes.description: Concentrate America's preferential programmes on Beijing. A stronger Chinese relationship gives Washington a credible alternative when seeking concessions from Moscow. Ordinary Soviet consultations remain available.
nodes.strategy: Strengthen the Chinese alternative, demonstrate that it is real, then ask Moscow for a better settlement.
requirements: An accepted Chinese civilian exchange programme.
Mutually exclusive with Consolidate Détente.
effects: Unlocks the China-priority industrial and security offers.

nodes.title: Consolidate Détente
nodes.description: Concentrate America's preferential programmes on an agreement with Moscow. Economic cooperation and negotiated strategic limits can secure Soviet concessions. Ordinary Chinese contacts remain available.
nodes.strategy: Offer Moscow a substantial stake in restraint and make clear to Beijing that Washington has another viable partner.
requirements: A jointly observed investment agreement includes the scientific programme.
Mutually exclusive with Play the China Card.

own.duration: while the qualifying joint programme remains in force

effects: Unlocks the Soviet-priority trade and arms-control offers.

treaty.term: US preferential programme; the Soviet government retains its own negotiating choices.
treaty.lifecycle: The priority spirit and weekly funding pause if joint participation ends. Restoration does not repeat the setup payment.

nodes.title: Civilian Industry Mission
nodes.description: Offer China a larger civilian technical mission with American financing. The agreement strengthens Chinese civilian development and American influence while increasing Chinese exposure to foreign involvement.
nodes.strategy: Build an attractive Chinese partnership that remains useful even if Moscow rejects the next American proposal.
requirements: Play the China Card is active.
China accepts the mission and its funding terms.

nodes.title: Strategic Consultations
nodes.description: Offer regular strategic consultations and defensive intelligence exchanges with Beijing. The agreement supports a shared assessment of Soviet pressure without transferring Chinese foreign policy to Washington.
nodes.strategy: Raise the strategic value of the American opening to China before approaching Moscow with new terms.
requirements: Play the China Card is active.
China accepts the consultation arrangement.

nodes.title: Grain and Credit
nodes.description: Use a Commercial Accord to expand civilian trade with Moscow. Attach an explicitly funded supply programme to the paper. Any credit is negotiated separately through the ordinary loan channel.
nodes.strategy: Make cooperation commercially valuable, giving Washington something concrete to expand or withhold in later negotiations.
requirements: Consolidate Détente is selected.
Both governments sign the commercial protocol and its civilian supply programme.

nodes.title: Arms-Control Talks
nodes.description: Prepare a SALT I paper in the standing arms-control channel. Negotiate bomb-production restraint and, if selected, retirement of named stored missile models. A separate ABM paper provides strategic-defence consultations.
nodes.strategy: Exchange American restraint for a reciprocal Soviet commitment, reducing the political cost of continued strategic competition.
requirements: Consolidate Détente is selected.
Both governments sign the reviewed SALT paper and its strategic consultations programme.
Stored missile retirement, if added, lists each covered model and its exact quantity before signature.

treaty.term: Opening SALT terms: bomb production -10%, no reserve retirement, until withdrawal. Delegations may revise before submission.

nodes.title: Signal Moscow
nodes.description: With Chinese approval, announce the public scope of a signed American-Chinese agreement and invite Moscow to negotiate improved terms. The Soviet response remains its own political decision.
nodes.strategy: Use an existing Chinese agreement as evidence that Washington has a credible alternative.
requirements: At least one enhanced Chinese agreement is active.
China approves publication of the joint statement.
effects: Publishes only the agreed joint statement.
nodes.history: Historical signalling precedent; proposed decision chain

treaty.agenda: US proposal to the existing Soviet negotiating channel
treaty.term: A Chinese agreement may inform Washington's offer; Moscow must decide for itself.
treaty.lifecycle: Public Chinese cooperation does not force a Soviet response or disclose secret Soviet activities.

nodes.title: Offer a Wider Settlement
nodes.description: Build on an accepted Soviet agreement and invite a broader political settlement. A joint announcement can demonstrate the value of the Soviet channel to Beijing while Chinese consultations continue.
nodes.strategy: Use concrete progress with Moscow to seek better terms from the other American diplomatic channel.
requirements: A jointly observed Commercial Accord or SALT agreement includes the corresponding enhanced programme.
The Soviet Union approves the additional joint statement.
effects: Publishes only the agreed joint statement.
nodes.history: Historical signalling precedent; proposed decision chain

treaty.agenda: Signed treaty register + agreed joint statement
treaty.term: Treaty signature already produces its own international announcement.
treaty.lifecycle: The focus proposes an additional political statement. A signature notification alone does not authorise it.

nodes.title: Link Benefits to Restraint
nodes.description: Offer additional civilian cooperation for a concrete regional concession. With Moscow, name each government's mission recipient and negotiate recall of its own attaches and volunteers through a Regional Stand-down paper.
nodes.strategy: Turn America's alternative relationship into a specific negotiated concession, rather than an automatic penalty on a rival.
requirements: A completed public diplomatic signal.
The paper names each government's own mission recipient and the selected withdrawal protocol.
The recipient approves all economic benefits, costs and regional concessions.

nodes.title: Maintain the American Balance
nodes.description: Review the standing American commitments in the treaty register and prepare revised terms through the same negotiating channel. Use the intelligence dossier to assess disclosed Soviet activity when deciding what Washington should offer next.
nodes.strategy: Keep competing agreements useful without making incompatible promises or treating a refusal as the end of American diplomacy.
requirements: The linkage framework has been established.
effects: Unlocks review of the preferential American programme.

treaty.term: Renegotiated concessions require a fresh reviewed paper and Soviet signature.
treaty.lifecycle: The dossier uses actual disclosed actions and native intelligence access. Revised offers preserve standing obligations until a new agreement is concluded.

detente_integration.status: Design bridge only, not installed gameplay
detente_integration.native: Existing treaty authoring, revision, consent, concessions, membership, expiry, withdrawal, register and news.
detente_integration.proposed: Attach the new research, supply and consultations programmes and their GDP-based funding to explicitly reviewed treaty terms. Existing treaty code does not yet contain these programme clauses.
detente_integration.tension: Existing reversible relief only: -1 point per jointly observed USA/SOV instrument, capped at -5. No additional focus-completion relief.
guards: A focus never signs a treaty for another country.
Do not replace a pending paper or reset a standing instrument.
Relevant joint membership and selected protocols are required, not only the focus receipt.
Programme suspension ends the associated weekly funding on both sides. No repeated setup payments or replayed assets.
Termination and a fresh instrument require new review; historical optional programme state cannot silently transfer to a new revision.
Use the strongest actual trade, investment and bomb-production protocol; do not stack copies.
Ending shared participation is not a blanket treaty breach verdict or an automatic sanction.
